subject: series
synopsis: A Warren Ellis miniseries with supernatural horror and psychological thriller elements.
author: Warren Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: A Warren Ellis horror miniseries exploring dark supernatural themes.
author: Warren Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: Christopher Priest's 2023 limited series exploring Superman stranded in deep space, cut off from Earth for 20 years in subjective time while only months pass for Lois. Priest used the prolonged isolation to examine Clark's psychology and the strain on his marriage with unusual depth.
author: Christopher Priest

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2019 series starring Lin Lie, a young Chinese man wielding an ancient sword with supernatural powers, introduced as part of Marvel's expansion into new Asian markets with original Chinese hero content.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Collected and colorized reprints of the original black-and-white Tank Girl strips from Deadline magazine, presenting Jamie Hewlett and Alan Martin's anarchic punk antiheroine stories with new color treatment for contemporary readers.
author: Alan Martin

subject: series
synopsis: Ted McKeever's apocalyptic Epic Comics series set in a decaying urban landscape where strange supernatural forces converge on a cast of broken and bizarre characters. McKeever's fractured, expressionistic art style gives the material a unique visual personality that rewards patient readers.
author: Ted McKeever

subject: series
synopsis: An all-ages IDW comic series adapting the classic 1987 TMNT cartoon, featuring the original animated Turtles in fun standalone adventures. Captures the lighthearted retro spirit of the Saturday morning cartoon.

subject: series
synopsis: Nagabe's gentle dark fairy tale: Shiva, a little girl, lives in the cursed Outside with Teacher, a horned creature whose touch could curse her.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1992 techno-thriller series by Lewis Shiner about a computer security specialist who uncovers a vast corporate conspiracy through his hacking skills. An early comics attempt to grapple seriously with the emerging digital world and computer crime.
author: Lewis Shiner

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's retrospective anthology collecting earlier Death's Head (the sardonic robotic freelance peacekeeping agent) appearances, assembled to satisfy demand for the breakout character after his success in Marvel UK titles.
author: Simon Furman

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2007 series by C.B. Cebulski following a support group of former teen superheroes trying to lead normal lives — Spider-Woman (Mattie Franklin), Darkhawk, Turbo, and others — who keep getting pulled back into adventure despite their intentions to quit.
author: C.B. Cebulski

subject: series
synopsis: Vicente Segrelles' stunning fantasy painted series following an unnamed mercenary who rides a magnificent dragon-like creature in a beautifully rendered pre-industrial world — landmark for its photorealistic painted art.
author: Vicente Segrelles

subject: series
synopsis: DC's digital series introducing Tim Fox as the new Batman of Gotham City in the near-future, expanding on John Ridley's Future State storyline about the first Black Batman. An important representation milestone given narrative depth by Ridley.
author: John Ridley

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Carey and Peter Gross's metafictional exploration of Tom Taylor, the son of a famous fantasy novelist whose fictional character he may actually be. A layered meditation on the power of stories.
author: Mike Carey

subject: series
synopsis: Si Spencer's 2007 Vertigo series following a team of London music scene veterans who solve supernatural crimes connected to the underground music world. A stylish genre mix that never quite found the audience it deserved in its 12-issue run.
author: Si Spencer

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Peyer and Jamal Igle's series in which a dark, gritty superhero and his campy counterpart switch Earths — a smart, affectionate deconstruction of superhero tonal extremes.
author: Tom Peyer

subject: series
synopsis: ABC anthology companion to the main Tom Strong series, featuring backup stories and alternate takes on Moore's pulp science hero; variable quality but includes interesting experiments with the character and his world.

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's collected editions of the second phase of their Transformers continuity, which became one of the most sophisticated and politically complex versions of the franchise, examining the Autobot-Decepticon war with new moral ambiguity.
author: John Barber

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's X-Men anthology collecting various Krakoa-era storylines, serving as a companion to the main X-line while spotlighting characters and subplots that don't fit in the flagship books.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Kevin Maguire's 1997 Acclaim superhero comedy about three sisters who become reluctant heroines.

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and Sara Pichelli's 2011 Ultimate Comics Spider-Man: Brooklyn teen Miles Morales gains spider powers and takes up the mantle after Peter Parker's death.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: The relaunched Ultimate X-Men series following the Ultimatum event, following a persecuted mutant population under government control; part of the Divided We Fall, United We Stand crossover.
author: Brian Wood

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series featuring the Ultimate Spider-Man in adventures for the Marvel Unlimited platform, tied to the character's modern Ultimate universe revival.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Gail Simone's excellent six-issue 2005 Infinite Crisis tie-in following the Secret Six — a ragtag team of B-list villains who refuse to join Lex Luthor's Society — as they face impossible odds. The origin of Simone's beloved Secret Six ensemble.
author: Gail Simone

subject: series
synopsis: A companion miniseries to the War of Kings cosmic event following Darkhawk's transformation and ascension into the cosmic-powered Raptor armor, bridging street-level hero into Marvel's interstellar war.
author: C.B. Cebulski

subject: series
synopsis: A miniseries revisiting untold chapters of Wolverine's history, filling in gaps from his past that intersect with major Marvel events and characters in ways that recontextualize his long life.

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Jenkins and Andy Kubert's prestige series finally revealing Wolverine's true origins as James Howlett in 19th-century Canada, a long-awaited mystery conclusion with painted art that redefined the character's history.
author: Paul Jenkins

subject: series
synopsis: Dav Pilkey's hugely popular kids' graphic novels about Dog Man, a crime-fighting part-dog, part-cop, and his nemesis Petey the cat.

subject: series
synopsis: A crossover miniseries featuring Marvel's demonic villain Mephisto challenging various superhero teams including the X-Men and Fantastic Four, testing their souls and values.
author: Al Milgrom

subject: series
synopsis: DC's Batman in Detective Comics across various collected volumes, encompassing James Tynion IV's acclaimed run featuring Batwoman and a rotating cast of Gotham heroes fighting religious cults and the Joker War's aftermath. Tynion's run is particularly notable for building Gotham's supporting cast into a full ensemble.
author: James Tynion IV

subject: series
synopsis: Kurt Busiek and Erik Larsen's 2001 Defenders: Doctor Strange, Hulk, Namor and Silver Surfer are cursed to reunite by Yandroth.

subject: series
synopsis: Yuu Watase's prequel to Fushigi Yugi: in 1923, Takiko Okuda is drawn into the Universe of the Four Gods as the priestess of Genbu.

subject: series
synopsis: Marv Wolfman's 1996 Night Force revival: Baron Winter again gathers reluctant agents against supernatural threats.

subject: series
synopsis: Acclaim's 1997 Ninjak relaunch: a teenage video-game fan gains ninja powers, a new take on the Valiant hero.

subject: series
synopsis: Osamu Tezuka's life work: linked tales across past and future eras, each touched by the immortal firebird and humanity's longing for eternal life.

subject: series
synopsis: Denny O'Neil and Michael Kaluta's atmospheric 1973 DC revival of Walter Gibson's pulp avenger, Lamont Cranston.

subject: series
synopsis: Fantagraphics' complete reprint of Floyd Gottfredson's Mickey Mouse newspaper adventure strips (1930-1955).

subject: series
synopsis: The New 52 Suicide Squad: Amanda Waller's Task Force X with Harley Quinn, Deadshot, King Shark and El Diablo.

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Verheiden and Mark A. Nelson's 1988 Dark Horse sequel to Aliens: Hicks and Newt face a xenomorph-ravaged Earth.
author: Mark Verheiden

subject: series
synopsis: Jay Faerber's 1999 New Warriors revival with a reunited teen team.

subject: series
synopsis: Steve Niles's 2011 IDW ongoing: Alice Blood sets out to prove vampires exist in the 30 Days of Night world.

subject: series
synopsis: Harvey Pekar's 2006 Vertigo American Splendor mini, more autobiographical stories of his Cleveland life.

subject: series
synopsis: Sarah Byam's 1993 Black Canary ongoing, Dinah Lance's short-lived solo series.

subject: series
synopsis: Charlton's 1965 Captain Atom by Steve Ditko: Air Force scientist Allen Adam becomes the atomic hero.

subject: series
synopsis: Brubaker and Phillips's 2019 Criminal ongoing: Cruel Summer's interlocking 1980s crime story of Teeg and Ricky Lawless.

subject: series
synopsis: Karl Kesel and Skottie Young's 2003 Human Torch solo series, Johnny Storm's hot-headed adventures.

subject: series
synopsis: Volume 2 of Image Comics' preview magazine of interviews and first looks.

subject: series
synopsis: Christopher Cantwell and CAFU's 2020 Iron Man: Tony Stark goes back to basics, then faces Korvac's cosmic ascension.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel Spotlight volume 2 (1979-1981), a short tryout series with Captain Marvel and other second-stringers.

subject: series
synopsis: Marv Wolfman's 2009 Vigilante: Adrian Chase's successor hunts criminals across the DC Universe.

subject: series
synopsis: Web of Spider-Man volume 2 (2009-2010), an anthology companion to Brand New Day's Amazing Spider-Man.

subject: series
synopsis: Antarctic Press's annual specials for Fred Perry's Gold Digger.

subject: series
synopsis: Action Lab's Danger Zone cheesecake horror: fangirl Katie Carva fights demons with a vampiric blade.

subject: series
synopsis: Action Lab's Danger Zone cheesecake horror: fangirl Katie Carva fights demons with a vampiric blade.

subject: series
synopsis: Josie Campbell's 2023 Amazons Attack: the Amazons are hunted after Wonder Woman's outlaw status in Dawn of DC.

subject: series
synopsis: Digital-first DC Super Hero Girls story for young readers.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel Tsunami's 2003 Namor: a teenage Namor's adventures, cancelled after 12 issues.

subject: series
synopsis: Brubaker and Phillips's Sleeper Season Two: Holden Carver's handler Lynch wakes from his coma, tightening the trap.

subject: series
synopsis: Goblin Slayer side-story manga of everyday adventures in the frontier town.

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Aaron's 2024 TMNT relaunch: the four brothers, scattered across the world, reunite to protect New York.

subject: series
synopsis: KaBoom!'s Peanuts comics: new stories and Schulz reprints of Charlie Brown, Snoopy and the gang.

subject: series
synopsis: Stephanie Phillips's 2024 Phoenix: Jean Grey roams the cosmos as the Phoenix.

subject: series
synopsis: Venom (2016-2018): Mike Costa's Lee Price arc, then Eddie Brock reunites with the symbiote, back to legacy #150.
author: Mike Costa, David Michelinie

subject: series
synopsis: Richard Sala's Fantagraphics series of macabre mystery-comedies, featuring Judy Drood and his gothic, deadpan adventure serials.

subject: series
synopsis: David Pepose's 2025 Dynamite revival of Hanna-Barbera's Space Ghost as a cosmic adventurer.
author: David Pepose

subject: series
synopsis: Kurt Busiek's Aquaman series introducing Arthur Joseph Curry as a new Aquaman while Arthur Orin/Orin navigated a strange undersea transformation. An interesting attempt to revitalize the franchise that was unfortunately interrupted by editorial changes.
author: Kurt Busiek

subject: series
synopsis: Larry Young's revival of his creator-owned AIT/Planet Lar sci-fi series, following a team of astronauts dealing with corporate conspiracies, space accidents, and moral compromises in near-future space exploration. A solid throwback to old-school sci-fi comics.
author: Larry Young

subject: series
synopsis: Nick Spencer's Avengers companion title during Hickman's run, filling in character-focused stories for the expanding Avengers roster while Hickman built his grand cosmological narrative.
author: Nick Spencer

subject: series
synopsis: Jeph Loeb's story in which a time-traveling Cable from a devastated future returns to our time to eliminate the Avengers before they can destroy his world.
author: Jeph Loeb

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison and Mark Millar's 1996 DC series following Uno, an Aztec warrior trained by a secret society and sent to Vanity City to prepare for a coming god-war. One of Morrison's early DC experiments before JLA, it mixed superhero mythology with Aztec spirituality and foreshadowed his later meta-narrative ambitions.
author: Grant Morrison, Mark Millar

subject: series
synopsis: Comic adaptations from the Babylon 5 science fiction television universe — DC and later Mongoose Publishing comics set aboard the iconic space station, featuring Commander Sinclair, Captain Sheridan, and the complex politics of a crucial interstellar waystation.

subject: series
synopsis: Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale's sequel to The Long Halloween, the landmark Batman mystery series, following up on the Holiday Killer mystery decades later. A long-awaited return to beloved characters in Loeb and Sale's distinctive noir style.
author: Jeph Loeb

subject: series
synopsis: Joshua Williamson and Andrei Bressan's fantasy series in which a young boy disappears into a fantasy realm and returns a year later — to his family — as a grown, battle-scarred warrior. But his family must determine whether the hero who returned is truly their son.
author: Joshua Williamson

subject: series
synopsis: A mature-audience tie-in to the Blood Hunt event with graphic content and dark themes.

subject: series
synopsis: Mohiro Kitoh's deeply dark mecha manga follows fifteen children who discover that agreeing to pilot a giant robot means one of them must die to power it after each battle. A relentlessly bleak and philosophically rigorous examination of sacrifice, meaning, and the adult world's exploitation of the young.
author: Mohiro Kitoh

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Smith's nine-volume fantasy epic follows the Bone cousins — hapless, funny Fone Bone and his equally hapless brothers — as they stumble into a war between ancient forces of dream and nightmare, building to one of the most satisfying conclusions in comics.
author: Jeff Smith

subject: series
synopsis: Bob Harras' 2005 DC series about Major Tim Zanetti, a soldier who becomes a conduit for extradimensional energy after a nuclear accident, giving him tremendous power at the cost of his ability to safely exist in our world. An underrated Infinite Crisis-era series with a genuinely tragic premise.
author: Bob Harras

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Kirkman's Image Comics series about an elderly superhero with an invulnerability power that makes him unkillable but can't stop him from aging — his adult son inherits the power and takes on the superhero role. A solid action series with an interesting intergenerational premise.
author: Robert Kirkman

subject: series
synopsis: Konami Kanata's irresistibly charming manga following Chi, a tiny kitten separated from her mother who is adopted by a young family. Drawn with the wide-eyed simplicity of a children's picture book but deeply observed in its portrayal of feline psychology, it achieved rare crossover appeal across age groups.
author: Konami Kanata

subject: series
synopsis: Vita Ayala's Children of the Atom series; diverse young mutant team with representation and depth.
author: Vita Ayala

subject: series
synopsis: Michel Fiffe's obsessively hand-drawn self-published series that began as a Suicide Squad pastiche and evolved into its own unique, wild creature. Every issue is entirely by Fiffe; the DIY energy is thrilling.
author: Michel Fiffe

subject: series
synopsis: Hugo Pratt's legendary series of poetic adventure graphic novels following the melancholy sailor Corto Maltese through the early 20th century's conflicts and exotic locales; one of the towering achievements of European comics, admired for Pratt's spare line-work and literary ambition.
author: Hugo Pratt

subject: series
synopsis: Defiant Comics' supernatural series from Jim Shooter's post-Valiant publishing venture, featuring Michael Alexander, a man who can sense supernatural threats, investigating occult conspiracies. Part of Defiant's brief but ambitious publishing line that ended with the company's closure.
author: Len Wein

subject: series
synopsis: Tim Seeley and Corin Howell's vampire story subverting expectations — a vampire in rural America confronted with the political polarization of his community and the question of what side he's on.
author: Tim Seeley

subject: series
synopsis: A five-issue crossover event by Geoff Johns in which the Spectre is separated from his human host and possessed by the demon Asmodel, threatening all of creation. It introduced Hal Jordan as the new host for the Spectre and set up the Spectre's story for years afterward.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1973–1975 horror anthology featuring short tales of terror, part of the broader explosion of horror anthology comics that filled Marvel's output during the Bronze Age following the loosening of the Comics Code.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Gerry Duggan's extended Deadpool run during the All-New All-Different Marvel era, following Wade Wilson at peak popularity as he navigates Avengers membership, fatherhood, and increasingly absurd threats.
author: Gerry Duggan

subject: series
synopsis: Mad Cave's 2024 Dick Tracy by Alex Segura and Michael Moreci: a modern noir reboot of Chester Gould's square-jawed detective.

subject: series
synopsis: Titan Comics' second year of Eleventh Doctor adventures, featuring Matt Smith's beloved incarnation in original storylines that expand the Doctor Who universe with new companions and threats. Captures the whimsical-dark energy of the Smith era effectively.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Titan Comics' series featuring Christopher Eccleston's Ninth Doctor in original adventures with Rose and Jack, capturing the raw energy and emotional directness of the 2005 revival before it found its full footing.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Titan Comics' second year of Twelfth Doctor adventures, featuring Peter Capaldi's cerebral incarnation in original comics stories that attempt to capture the character's unique blend of alien coldness and underlying compassion.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Raffaele Ienco's 2012 Image action thriller following a young woman with exceptional combat skills who becomes a target after witnessing something she shouldn't have — a stripped-down chase narrative that showcased Ienco's kinetic action art.
author: Raffaele Ienco

subject: series
synopsis: Warren Ellis and Ben Templesmith's crime procedural set in Snowtown, a decayed and lawless city, following Detective Richard Fell who is transferred there under murky circumstances and must work with almost no resources to solve disturbing cases.
author: Warren Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics' companion series spotlighting individual members of the FemForce, the publisher's flagship all-female superhero team. Primarily supplements the main FemForce series with origin stories and character studies aimed at established fans of the team.

subject: series
synopsis: A dark psychological manga by Kei Sanbe (creator of Erased) about twins who witness their parents' murder as children, with one twin surviving to become a detective obsessed with revenge while searching for his missing brother. Sanbe's characteristic mix of thriller plotting and childhood trauma is in full effect here, creating a bleak but compelling mystery.
author: Kei Sanbe

subject: series
synopsis: DC's early 1970s horror anthology hosted by Charity, the ghost of a young woman, in stories that followed the Edgar Allan Poe-inflected horror tradition popular at the time. Part of DC's horror anthology line alongside The Witching Hour and House of Mystery.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: The original crossover miniseries bringing together Freddy Krueger, Jason Voorhees, and Ash Williams from Evil Dead.

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman's 2023 series introducing a new cosmological framework for the Marvel Universe through the conflict between the natural and artificial orders, featuring dense world-building in Hickman's signature style with art by Valerio Schiti.
author: Jonathan Hickman

subject: series
synopsis: Elisabetta Dami's long-running children's graphic novel series following the mouse journalist Geronimo Stilton on fantasy adventures in the Kingdom of Fantasy.
author: Elisabetta Dami

subject: series
synopsis: André Franquin's beloved Belgian comic strip (known as Gaston Lagaffe in French) follows the lazy, catastrophe-prone office worker Gaston and his endless stream of absurd inventions and pranks. A masterwork of visual comedy and one of the pillars of the Franco-Belgian tradition.
author: André Franquin

subject: series
synopsis: An ongoing series in the GFT Wonderland sub-universe, continuing the dark reimagining of Lewis Carroll's Wonderland as a genuinely dangerous and monstrous realm. Follows characters navigating a corrupted, terrifying version of the classic fantasy world.

subject: series
synopsis: Tim Seeley's horror-comedy series following Cassie Hack and the gentle monster Vlad hunting supernatural slashers, deconstructing slasher movie conventions with genuine genre affection while developing real emotional depth in its mismatched leads.
author: Tim Seeley

subject: series
synopsis: Companion UK horror magazine to The House of Hammer, running concurrent with it and featuring similar comic adaptations and horror-themed content drawn from the Hammer Films library.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis' beloved DC series starring Tommy Monaghan, a Gotham hitman with low-level superpowers who only kills bad guys. Ennis balances visceral humor and genuine pathos across 60 issues, delivering some of the most memorably human storytelling in superhero comics — including the legendary 'Of Thee I Sing' Superman crossover.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: Rick Remender and Roland Boschi's Image Comics crime thriller about a professional boxer drawn into a violent conflict with white supremacist gangs. Fast and brutal with Remender's characteristic themes of working-class trauma.
author: Rick Remender

subject: series
synopsis: Sam Kieth's whimsical 2002 mini: Wolverine and the Hulk trek across the Arctic to rescue a strange little girl's father.

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid's Indestructible Hulk repositioned Bruce Banner as an asset rather than a threat, partnering with SHIELD to direct the Hulk's destruction productively; the Inhumanity tie-in issues see Banner navigating the Terrigen Mist outbreak.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid's chilling exploration of what would happen if the world's greatest superhero snapped — following the Plutonian's descent from iconic protector to unstoppable destroyer and the former allies scrambling to survive him.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: Tom King's DC Black Label limited series revisiting Jenny Sparks, the Spirit of the 20th Century from The Authority, following her across pivotal historical moments. King treats the Wildstorm character with the same literary weight he brings to his other revisionist superhero work.
author: Tom King

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's prequel series exploring Kato's backstory in Japan before becoming the Green Hornet's masked partner — his ninja training, early missions, and the events that shaped his extraordinary skills.
author: Ande Parks

subject: series
synopsis: Wes Craig's all-ages fantasy adventure — by the Deadly Class artist — following a young girl and her robot brother navigating a dangerous world of monsters and magic after their village is destroyed.
author: Wes Craig

subject: series
synopsis: Haruko Ichikawa's haunting manga about immortal gem-beings who must fight against alien Lunarians who harvest them for decorations. Spare, philosophical, and visually stunning — one of the most formally distinctive manga of the 2010s.
author: Haruko Ichikawa

subject: series
synopsis: Riko descends into a bottomless chasm filled with incredible relics and horrifying creatures, searching for her missing mother alongside the robot boy Reg. Tsukushi's manga pairs gorgeous art with escalating darkness and genuine worldbuilding depth.
author: Akihito Tsukushi

subject: series
synopsis: Man-Thing volume 2 (1979-1981): Michael Fleisher and Chris Claremont continue the swamp creature's Florida tales with Don Perlin art.

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024-2025 Marvel Zombies revival continuing the zombie alternate-universe concept, following a new cast through a fresh outbreak scenario while maintaining the horror-comedy genre blend that defined the original Marvel Zombies run.

subject: series
synopsis: The original British Marvelman strips from the 1950s, featuring the Captain Marvel-derived superhero in adventures for young readers. Historically significant as the character Alan Moore would later reimagine as Miracleman, transforming him into a work of dark complexity.
author: Mick Anglo

subject: series
synopsis: An independent biographical horror-drama comic retelling the life of Joseph Merrick, the so-called Elephant Man of Victorian England, examining his humanity and the society that both exploited and pitied him.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's quarterly anthology tie-in to its Midnight Sons horror imprint, collecting stories featuring Ghost Rider, Blaze, Morbius, Blade, and the Darkhold-related characters in self-contained horror adventures.

subject: series
synopsis: Amy Reeder and Brandon Montclare's delightful series starring Lunella Lafayette, a nine-year-old Inhuman genius who bonds with a time-displaced Tyrannosaurus rex in the Lower East Side. Celebrated for its all-ages appeal and STEM themes.
author: Amy Reeder, Brandon Montclare

subject: series
synopsis: Kazuo Koike and Hideki Mori's continuation of the legendary Lone Wolf and Cub saga, set in the Meiji era decades after the original story. Explores how Japan's modernization affects the samurai code as a new generation carries the tradition forward.
author: Kazuo Koike

subject: series
synopsis: Brandon Thomas's Catalyst Prime series follows David Powell, a man who awakes with no memories but extraordinary powers after a cosmic event that changed the world. Thomas brings genuine emotional intelligence to the superhero premise, building a diverse cast within Lion Forge's interconnected universe.
author: Brandon Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: DC's digital comedy series featuring Nightwing in humorous situations that lean into fan community culture around the character, including the longstanding appreciation for Dick Grayson's physique. Tongue-in-cheek fan service content.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Crime noir reimagining from Mad Cave Studios casting the Sheriff of Nottingham as a corrupt detective hunting a vigilante thief called Robin Hood in a brutal medieval setting.

subject: series
synopsis: Ahoy Comics' anthology series collecting cryptozoology-themed horror and sci-fi stories, using creatures like Bigfoot, the Loch Ness Monster, and other cryptids as the jumping-off point for creator-driven genre fiction.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Moore and J.H. Williams III's visually and intellectually extraordinary exploration of magic and mythology through the story of a college student who becomes the avatar of a mythological hero; Williams's page design is without peer in mainstream comics.
author: Alan Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Recent Valiant series following a team of powered individuals discovering they are part of an alien consciousness network — exploring cosmic-scale psionics in the current Valiant Universe.
author: Fred Van Lente

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Parker's series following Betty Ross as the Red She-Hulk, finding her own heroic identity outside the shadow of Bruce Banner. Parker brings his customary wit and forward momentum to a character who might otherwise have remained a gimmick.
author: Jeff Parker

subject: series
synopsis: Ryan Parrott and Abel's superhero series following a teenager who unwillingly inherits the mantle of Rogue Sun — a powerful solar-powered hero — from his estranged father, while also investigating his father's murder.
author: Ryan Parrott

subject: series
synopsis: Mitsuru Hattori's romantic horror comedy follows a zombie-obsessed boy whose new girlfriend accidentally becomes an actual zombie. Explores the comedy and tragedy of the premise with more emotional sincerity than its concept suggests.
author: Mitsuru Hattori

subject: series
synopsis: A Secret Invasion tie-in mini-series following the Inhumans as the Skrull infiltration reaches their royal family, forcing Black Bolt and his people to confront betrayal from within. The series connects into the broader War of Kings cosmic arc.
author: Joe Pokaski

subject: series
synopsis: A European crime thriller series following an undercover operative navigating the dangerous intersections of organized crime and intelligence work. Tautly plotted in the tradition of French polar procedurals, with strong atmosphere and morally complex characters.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's anthology series featuring Spider-Man team-ups with various Marvel heroes and villains, following in the tradition of Marvel Team-Up with standalone stories pairing Peter Parker with unexpected allies.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: The long-running Spider-Man/Deadpool buddy series pairing Marvel's two quip-masters for comedic team-up adventures that played their contrasting personalities for maximum laughs while delivering solid action. A fun but lightweight ongoing that knew its lane.
author: Joe Kelly

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 IDW/Marvel series following the Ewoks of Endor in all-ages adventures on and around their forest moon, expanding on the beloved creatures from Return of the Jedi.

subject: series
synopsis: Hardcover reprints of Doctor Strange from Ditko's Strange Tales origins through Englehart and Colan, Stern and Paul Smith.
author: Marv Wolfman

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 DC limited series featuring a new Suicide Squad lineup facing a threat calibrated to require exactly their morally flexible approach — a tight action-focused installment in the long-running Task Force X concept.

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Snyder and Jim Lee's prestige Superman series introducing Wraith, a Superman analog secretly working for the US government since WWII. Snyder's high-concept plotting and Lee's monumental art make for an ambitious if slightly overstuffed run.
author: Scott Snyder

subject: series
synopsis: Kintetsu Yamada's charming adult romance follows a woman who is extremely self-conscious about her heavy sweating and her unlikely romance with a soap developer who is fascinated by her scent. A warm, sensual, and unusually mature rom-com.
author: Kintetsu Yamada

subject: series
synopsis: A horror anthology series from the early 1990s in the tradition of EC Comics' horror anthologies, presenting short supernatural and horror tales with ironic twist endings.

subject: series
synopsis: James Tynion IV's New 52 spin-off from the Court of Owls storyline, following a former Talon assassin named Calvin Rose who escapes the Court and fights for his freedom.
author: James Tynion IV

subject: series
synopsis: A Marvel/Ultraverse crossover team series following Marvel's acquisition of Malibu Comics, mixing Ultraverse characters with Marvel heroes in shared adventures. The structural awkwardness of post-acquisition crossovers limits the series' coherence.
author: Ian Edginton

subject: series
synopsis: Joshua Fialkov and Joe Infurnari's thriller about five friends who bury a time capsule and discover letters from their future selves warning them about the apocalypse they will cause. A character-driven science fiction series about choice, complicity, and whether the future can be changed.
author: Joshua Fialkov

subject: series
synopsis: Satoshi Wagahara's manga adaptation follows the Demon Lord Satan, defeated by the Hero, who escapes to modern Tokyo and works at a fast food restaurant while trying to reconquer the world. A reliably funny fish-out-of-water comedy.
author: Satoshi Wagahara

subject: series
synopsis: Kazuo Umezu's classic survival horror manga follows an entire elementary school that is suddenly transported to a desolate post-apocalyptic wasteland. A seminal work of horror manga showcasing the imagination of one of the genre's founding masters.
author: Kazuo Umezu

subject: series
synopsis: Daisuke Aizawa's isekai parody follows a boy who always wanted to be a 'background character pulling strings in secret' and is reincarnated into a fantasy world where he creates a fictional secret organization — that turns out to be real. A clever meta-comedy of chuunibyou power fantasies.
author: Daisuke Aizawa

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1996 4-issue event featuring the Sun-Eater threatening to consume the sun, prompting the sacrifice of Hal Jordan to reignite it -- a landmark moment in the Parallax/Green Lantern saga. The core story is emotionally effective even if the event structure dilutes impact.
author: Karl Kesel

subject: series
synopsis: Shuzo Oshimi's psychologically intense coming-of-age story follows a bookish boy who steals his crush's gym clothes and is blackmailed into a disturbing relationship by the class outcast. A claustrophobically compelling portrait of adolescent shame, deviance, and self-discovery.
author: Shuzo Oshimi
